newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France head wants sell-off by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Air France head wants sell-off by 1998.

text.p: The chairman of Air France has written in a house magazine that he would like the state carrier to be sold by early next year, with staff holding 20 to 30 percent.

"My wish is that we can privatise before the end of 1997, or at the start of 1998, because for a commercial enterprise having a state shareholder is a brake on development," Christian Blanc wrote in the magazine France Aviation, received on Friday.
"I would also like employees to control a large part of the capital -- 20 to 30 percent -- so that they can have an overall view of the company and its development," he said.
He said the state should keep a minority stake in a company that would remain of national strategic importance.
Air France is due for privatisation and timing of the sale partly depends on the 1996 results. Blanc has forecast the company would break even in 1997.
French newspapers reported earlier this month that Blanc had criticised state "interference" in Air France and said he was an ardent advocate of privatisation.
In the house magazine article, Blanc said labour relations would be a key issue for Air France over the next three years.
If a pattern of recent strikes continued, gains from the airline's recent restructuring work would be lost, he said.
